title: Truncation tower reconstructs a complex under bounded local cohomological dimension

from.place: proof, first step, truncation tower (via Stacks 08D3)

statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume there exist an integer $d\geq0$ and a basis $\mathcal B$ for the topology of $X$ such that $H^p(U,H^q(E))=0$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$, all $p>d$ and all $q<0$, where $H^q(E)$ is the $q$-th cohomology sheaf and $H^p(U,-)$ is sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on $U$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. For $n\geq0$ let $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$ be the standard truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], with their canonical transition maps $E_{n+1}\to E_n$ and the canonical maps $E\to E_n$. Then $E$, together with a morphism $E\to\prod_nE_n$ whose components are the canonical maps, is a derived limit $R\varprojlim_nE_n$ in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]; that is, the canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_nE_n$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 0D64, label lemma-is-limit-dimension (stated there for a ringed space; specialized here to a scheme)

proof.text: For each point $x\in X$, let $\mathfrak U_x=\{U\in\mathcal B\mid x\in U\}$; because $\mathcal B$ is a basis this is a fundamental system of open neighborhoods. Define $p_x(m)=d+\max(0,m)$. If $U\in\mathfrak U_x$, $p>p_x(m)$, and $m-p<0$, then $p>d$, so the assumed vanishing gives $H^p(U,H^{m-p}(E))=0$. If $m-p\geq0$, then $p\leq m\leq\max(0,m)+d$ contradicts $p>p_x(m)$ (and when $m<0$ this case is impossible). Thus the hypotheses of [lem-pc-ringed-space-pointwise-truncation-limit] hold (a scheme is a ringed space). The product $\prod_nE_n$ exists in $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [lem-pc-ringed-space-derived-products], so the system $(E_n)$ has a derived limit $(K,p_K,\delta_K)$ [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence, part (1)]. By [lem-pc-ringed-space-pointwise-truncation-limit] there is $c:E\to K$ with $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ p_K\circ c$ the canonical map $E\to E_n$ for all $n$, and $c$ is an isomorphism. Put $p=p_K\circ c:E\to\prod_nE_n$, whose components are the canonical maps, and $\delta=c[1]^{-1}\circ\delta_K$. Then $(c,\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$ is an isomorphism from the triangle $E\xrightarrow{p}\prod_nE_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nE_n\xrightarrow{\delta}E[1]$ to the Roos triangle of $K$, so the former is distinguished (triangles isomorphic to distinguished ones are distinguished [def-weil-triangulated-category]); hence $(E,p,\delta)$ is a derived limit of $(E_n)$, and the canonical map $E\to R\varprojlim_nE_n$ (namely $c$) is an isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Split the uniform cohomological-dimension truncation theorem by introducing the strictly more general pointwise criterion of Stacks Tag 0D62 and instantiating it with the constant bound p_x(m)=d+max(0,m) on basis neighborhoods.
